macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Hot U.S. inflation pushes stocks lower and raises Fed hike risks
items.summary: U.S. CPI rose 0.4% month over month in October, above the 0.3% consensus forecast, while core CPI increased 0.3% versus expectations of 0.2%. The data strengthened expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate increase and raised concern about a potentially more aggressive tightening cycle.

items.title: Major U.S. indexes finish lower after inflation report
items.summary: The Dow fell 0.3% to 52,231.89, the S&P 500 declined 0.4% to 7,520.93, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.7% to 25,065.88. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.99% from 4.87% as markets priced in greater policy risk.

items.title: Fed official signals possible half-point December hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he supported a quarter-point rate increase in December even if inflation cooled, and that a 50-basis-point hike should be considered if underlying inflation remained elevated. Futures markets subsequently priced roughly a 91% probability of a quarter-point December increase and about 9% for a half-point move.

items.title: Nvidia leads technology-sector selloff
items.summary: Nvidia fell about 5.5% and had declined nearly 9.6% over two sessions, weighing heavily on the S&P 500. The broader S&P technology sector dropped 1.4% amid renewed pressure on artificial-intelligence-related stocks.

items.title: CoreWeave shares rise after earnings; Anthropic IPO plans expand
items.summary: CoreWeave shares gained about 5.6% in evening trading after its results helped lift S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures. Anthropic disclosed plans to offer 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, while reports indicated the company could seek a larger offering and higher valuation.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: U.S. Treasury bars financial institutions from dealing with MEXC
items.summary: FinCEN designated Seychelles-incorporated crypto exchange MEXC Global as a primary money-laundering concern linked to Russian illicit finance. U.S. financial institutions will be barred from transferring funds to or from MEXC beginning December 10, while MEXC says it has contacted FinCEN and will cooperate.[4][6]

items.title: Major cryptocurrencies decline over 24 hours
items.summary: Bitcoin was trading near $73,600, down about 1.3%, while ether was near $2,060, down 2.6%, and Solana near $83, down 3.4%.[1] Another market update reported bitcoin down 2.1% and ether down 3.8%, indicating broad weakness among leading assets.[6]

items.title: MARA sells 13,597 bitcoin to repay debt
items.summary: Bitcoin miner MARA sold 13,597 BTC and repaid $750 million in debt. The company also authorized a $500 million stock buyback and said two planned data-center leases could be delayed until 2027.[6]

items.title: Gram rises while broader crypto market falls
items.summary: Gram, the native token of Telegram’s blockchain, gained about 4.5% over 24 hours to around $1.15, standing out amid declines in major cryptocurrencies. Its reported market capitalization was approximately $3.28 billion.[2]

items.title: Blockchain.com launches institutional API trading service
items.summary: Blockchain.com announced an institutional API trading service intended to provide eligible clients with automated, around-the-clock access to principal crypto liquidity through a single API. Public reporting did not disclose detailed fees or legal terms.[1]

items.title: Ethersphere software package reportedly compromised
items.summary: Security researchers at Socket reported that malicious code was implanted in Ethersphere’s bee-js package and Swarm Desktop application, potentially targeting users’ wallet keys.[6]

items.title: Ukraine central bank rejects crypto bill in current form
items.summary: Ukraine’s central bank said it could not support draft law 10225-d as written, citing risks involving uncontrolled admission of foreign tokens, regulatory gaps that could enable arbitrage, and licensing discretion that could encourage monopolization or corruption.[1]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google expands Gemini 4 Carbon rollout
items.summary: Google reportedly opened Gemini 4 Carbon to developers, enterprises, scientists, and paid AI Ultra users after an earlier limited release. The model targets autonomous, multi-step workflows, while Google also previewed multi-agent coordination in Antigravity.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Ember for repetitive agent tasks
items.summary: Meta introduced Muse Ember, a smaller and lower-cost model designed for tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long-document parsing. The model is available through Meta’s Model API and Muse Code.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly launched Claude Fable 5.2 for general users and Claude Mythos 5.2 for vetted cybersecurity and biology organizations, alongside a reported 20% price reduction.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces AlphaProof Code
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced AlphaProof Code, an agent system for formal software verification. The system reportedly proved security properties in code implementing the Signal protocol using Lean.

items.title: Sapiens reports major reduction in robotics training time
items.summary: Singapore startup Sapiens Technology says its parameter-efficient training method can reduce robotics model training from months to roughly 30 minutes in some cases. The company is discussing pilots with robotics and medical firms in several countries.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Businesses beta
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly introduced business-facing features including company profiles, a business hub, and agents that can interact with users for tasks such as comparison shopping.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony reportedly cancels Fairgames live-service shooter
items.summary: Sony has reportedly canceled Fairgames, a live-service shooter in development at Haven Studios, after testing failed to meet the company’s expectations.

items.title: Nearly half of new Steam games reportedly use AI
items.summary: Approximately 49.9% of games released on Steam in October reportedly used generative AI in areas such as coding, artwork, or voice work, highlighting the technology’s rapid adoption and ongoing community backlash.

items.title: US lawmakers propose bill addressing digital game ownership
items.summary: Representative Ritchie Torres has proposed the Power to the Players Act, legislation intended to address consumer rights and long-term access to digitally purchased games as publishers reduce reliance on physical media.

items.title: Take-Two CEO comments on Zelda remake and GTA 6 competition
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick praised Nintendo’s reported Ocarina of Time remake while discussing whether it competes with Rockstar’s GTA 6, scheduled for release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: Logitech gives employees a gaming day ahead of GTA 6
items.summary: Logitech is reportedly offering its roughly 7,000 employees a paid day off to play games, including GTA 6, as part of an initiative called Logi Game Day.
